definition: The unit for amount of substance (mol). A mole of anything holds exactly the Avogadro constant's number of the stated particles, such as atoms, molecules or ions.
The number of particles in one mole, $N_\text{A} = \pu{6.02e23 mol-1}$ in the data booklet. Its unit, mol⁻¹, means "per mole".
$M_\text{r}$: the sum of the relative atomic masses of all the atoms in a formula, compared with one-twelfth of the mass of a carbon-12 atom. It has no units.
$M$: the mass of one mole of a substance, in g mol⁻¹. It has the same value as the relative formula mass, $M_\text{r}$, or the relative atomic mass for atoms.
